6. Gamma Function and Related Functions. Mathematical Properties.
6.1. Gamma (Factorial) Function.
Euler's Integral
6.1.1  \Gamma(z)=\int_0^\infty t^{z-1}e^{-t}\,dt \quad (\Re z>0)
       =k^z\int_0^\infty t^{z-1}e^{-kt}\,dt \quad (\Re z>0,\ \Re k>0)
Euler's Formula
6.1.2  \Gamma(z)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{n!\,n^{z}}{z(z+1)\cdots(z+n)} \quad (z\neq 0,-1,-2,\dots)
Euler's Infinite Product
6.1.3  \frac{1}{\Gamma(z)}=z e^{\gamma z}\prod_{n=1}^{\infty}\left[\left(1+\frac{z}{n}\right)e^{-z/n}\right] \quad (|z|<\infty)
       \gamma=\lim_{m\to\infty}\left[1+\frac12+\frac13+\frac14+\cdots+\frac1m-\ln m\right]=.57721\,56649\dots
\gamma is known as Euler's constant and is given to 25 decimal places in chapter 1. \Gamma(z) is single valued and analytic over the entire complex plane, save for the points z=-n\ (n=0,1,2,\dots) where it possesses simple poles with residue (-1)^n/n!. Its reciprocal 1/\Gamma(z) is an entire function possessing simple zeros at the points z=-n\ (n=0,1,2,\dots).
Hankel's Contour Integral
6.1.4  \frac{1}{\Gamma(z)}=\frac{i}{2\pi}\int_C (-t)^{-z}e^{-t}\,dt \quad (|z|<\infty)
The path of integration C starts at +\infty on the real axis, circles the origin in the counterclockwise direction and returns to the starting point.
Factorial and \Pi Notations
6.1.5  \Pi(z)=z!=\Gamma(z+1)
Integer Values
6.1.6  \Gamma(n+1)=1\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdots(n-1)n=n!
6.1.7  \lim_{z\to n}\frac{1}{\Gamma(-z)}=0=\frac{1}{(-n-1)!} \quad (n=0,1,2,\dots)
Fractional Values
6.1.8  \Gamma(\tfrac12)=2\int_0^\infty e^{-t^2}\,dt=\pi^{1/2}=1.77245\,38509\dots=(-\tfrac12)!
6.1.9  \Gamma(\tfrac32)=\tfrac12\pi^{1/2}=.88622\,69254\dots=(\tfrac12)!
6.1.10 \Gamma(n+\tfrac14)=\frac{1\cdot 5\cdot 9\cdot 13\cdots(4n-3)}{4^n}\Gamma(\tfrac14),\quad \Gamma(\tfrac14)=3.62560\,99082\dots
6.1.11 \Gamma(n+\tfrac13)=\frac{1\cdot 4\cdot 7\cdot 10\cdots(3n-2)}{3^n}\Gamma(\tfrac13),\quad \Gamma(\tfrac13)=2.67893\,85347\dots
6.1.12 \Gamma(n+\tfrac12)=\frac{1\cdot 3\cdot 5\cdot 7\cdots(2n-1)}{2^n}\Gamma(\tfrac12)
6.1.13 \Gamma(n+\tfrac23)=\frac{2\cdot 5\cdot 8\cdot 11\cdots(3n-1)}{3^n}\Gamma(\tfrac23),\quad \Gamma(\tfrac23)=1.35411\,79394\dots
6.1.14 \Gamma(n+\tfrac34)=\frac{3\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 15\cdots(4n-1)}{4^n}\Gamma(\tfrac34),\quad \Gamma(\tfrac34)=1.22541\,67024\dots

7.3.27  \pi zf(z)\sim1+\sum_{m=1}^{\infty} (-1)^m\frac{1\cdot3\cdots(4m-1)}{(\pi z^2)^{2m}} \quad (z\to\infty,|\arg z|<\tfrac{\pi}{2})

If R_n^{(f)}(z), R_n^{(g)}(z) are the remainders after n terms in 7.3.27, 7.3.28, respectively, then
7.3.29  R_n^{(f)}(z)=(-1)^n\frac{1\cdot3\cdots(4n-1)}{(\pi z^2)^{2n}}\theta^{(f)},\quad \theta^{(f)}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(2n+\frac12)}\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t}t^{2n-\frac12}}{1+\left(\frac{2t}{\pi z^2}\right)^2}dt \quad (|\arg z|<\tfrac{\pi}{4})
7.3.30  R_n^{(g)}(z)=(-1)^n\frac{1\cdot3\cdots(4n+1)}{(\pi z^2)^{2n}}\theta^{(g)},\quad \theta^{(g)}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(2n+\frac32)}\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t}t^{2n+\frac12}}{1+\left(\frac{2t}{\pi z^2}\right)^2}dt \quad (|\arg z|<\tfrac{\pi}{4})
7.3.31  |\theta^{(f)}|<1,\ |\theta^{(g)}|<1 \quad (|\arg z|\le\tfrac{\pi}{8})
For x real, R_n^{(f)}(x) and R_n^{(g)}(x) are less in absolute value than the first neglected term and of the same sign.

7.4.5  \int_0^\infty t^{2n+1}e^{-at^2}dt=\frac{n!}{2a^{n+1}} \quad (\Re a>0;n=0,1,2,\dots)
